title: Mapping data flows against notebooks: when each one wins

videos.script: Quitanda's night has to be cleaned before anyone can trust it. Orders sent twice, payments in any case, totals with a comma. {{dirty}} On Azure there are two common ways to write that cleaning. {{two}} A mapping data flow draws it as boxes, and Data Factory turns the boxes into Spark on a cluster it starts. {{boxes}} A notebook writes it as code, and runs it on Spark in Synapse, Fabric or Databricks. {{code}} Neither runs without Azure. So you will write the night as code, and run it on your laptop over Azurite, with DuckDB doing Spark's part. {{laptop}} Then you will test it on four rows, and watch a plausible shortcut fail the test. {{test}} A data flow cannot be tested that way. It needs a cluster every time. {{cluster}} And the clock. A cluster takes minutes to start, and keeping it warm costs minutes too. {{clock}} By the end you will know when the boxes win, when the code wins, and when the night needs no cluster at all. {{choice}}
